title: regime_overhaul: /frameworksInScope
description: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 is still in frameworksInScope, but for NBFCs RBI repealed it on 28 Nov 2025. It was replaced by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025 (RBI/DOR/2025-26/363). Chapter IV and the IT-specific provisions of Chapter II apply to NBFCs in the Middle Layer and above, and this entity's RBI registration N-13.09999 is nbfc-middle-layer. The successor has no vocab id and no instruments.json entry lists rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 in supersedes[], so instrument_superseded cannot be expressed. The profile is left unchanged and the regime change is flagged for re-review. Timing caveat: the repeal predates the catalog retrievedAt (2026-09-14), and the catalog version string already records it. It is reported because the profile was never refreshed and the repeal falls inside the 24-month window. Third-party IT and cyber arrangements outside the outsourcing directions fall under rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 paras 126-135, which is already in scope. From: rbi-it-outsourcing-md-2023 (in scope as a binding instrument). To: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025, RBI/DOR/2025-26/363 (no vocab id). Effective date: 2025-11-28.

description: src/tools/args.ts's zEJSON() (lines 78-90, used for find/export filters and every non-vector-search aggregation stage) is `z.object({}).loose()` with no maxItems on the enclosing pipeline array and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values; DBOperationArgs.database and CollOperationArgs.collection (mongodbTool.ts:11-17) are plain z.string() with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike CommonArgs.string()'s NO_UNICODE_REGEX in the same repo (args.ts:22-23). This is an input-validation gap on the tool-call surface, not a rate-limiting mechanism, which this codebase does not implement at all for MCP tool calls.

title: MongoDB MCP tool schemas carry no personal-data classification markers
description: src/tools/mongodb/mongodbSchemas.ts:1-107 (and, by extension, every mongodb/* tool argsShape it feeds) defines filter, projection, document and pipeline fields as opaque EJSON or `.passthrough()` records with only a `.describe()` prose hint (e.g. `zAutoEmbedVectorSearchStageParams`, `VectorSearchStage`). No field, in this file or anywhere under src/tools/mongodb, carries a data-classification annotation (x-data-classification, x-dpdp-category, @pii or equivalent), although applications/mcp-gateway/README.md and applications/mcp-gateway/env/{qa,prod}.json declare the connected client-data and order stores pii + financial. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0. zEJSON is defined as z.object({}).loose() in src/tools/args.ts:88-90; .passthrough() appears only in find.ts:22 and create/createIndex.ts:164, not in mongodbSchemas.ts itself.

title: find tool returns full unmasked documents from pii/financial collections
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/find.ts:108-118: FindTool.execute EJSON-serialises the entire cursor result set (`EJSON.stringify(cursorResults.documents)`) and returns it verbatim to the MCP client; the only applied limits are `config.maxBytesPerQuery` and `config.maxDocumentsPerQuery`, neither of which masks or filters fields. env/qa.json and env/prod.json both declare dataClassification [pii, financial] for this app. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: aggregate tool returns full unmasked pipeline results
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:187-192: AggregateTool.execute EJSON-serialises and returns the entire aggregation result set for an arbitrary user-supplied pipeline; pipelines containing `$out`/`$merge` (lines 134-141) write to a collection and send back no documents, so they are not an additional data-return path, but the read branch's result set still carries no masking or classification filter before being returned to the client. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: export tool writes full unmasked documents to an unencrypted local file
description: src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:68-98: ExportTool.execute streams the full find/aggregate cursor to a local JSON file via ExportsManager.createJSONExport with no field mask and no encryption-at-rest on the export file; the file is exposed to the caller via a resource URI and, on stdio transport (isServerRunningLocally(), lines 131-133), its plain filesystem path. Cleanup relies on ExportsManager.close() deleting the session export directory and a best-effort TTL sweep (config.exportTimeoutMs, default 300000ms), not immediate purge. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: CreateDBUserTool returns a newly generated password in plain text
description: src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:84-96: when the tool auto-generates a password, the success content text is `User "${username}" created successfully with password: \`${password}\`.`, sent as the raw JSON-RPC tool result. `this.session.keychain.register(password, "password")` runs immediately before, but keychain-based redaction (loggerBase.ts) only scrubs subsequent logger output, not the direct tool-result payload that reaches the MCP client transcript. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: MCP HTTP transport has no default authentication requirement
description: src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-319: setupMiddlewares() is the only request gate on the HTTP transport; it loops over `Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders)` and rejects a request only if a configured header value mismatches. `httpHeaders` defaults to `{}` (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143), so with no operator configuration the loop performs zero comparisons and `next()` is always called: every JSON-RPC tool call is reachable unauthenticated over HTTP once the transport binds beyond loopback (httpHost defaults to 127.0.0.1; the repo's AWS Dockerfile sets host 0.0.0.0 and the Azure bicep binds to '::'). Consistent with this, deploy/azure/bicep/params_template.json ships `authMode: NOAUTH` by default; a proper Azure-AD OIDC auth config exists only as an opt-in second template. env/prod.json lists this app's prod environment as exposure: partner with dataClassification [pii, financial]. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: Core MongoDB tool arguments accept unbounded, unvalidated input that reaches the driver
description: src/tools/args.ts:78-90: `zEJSON()` (`z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON)`) accepts any key/value pair with no maxItems on enclosing arrays (AggregateArgs.pipeline, defined at src/tools/mongodb/read/aggregate.ts:47-49) and no maxLength/pattern on keys or values, and is used as the schema for find/export `filter` and for every aggregation stage that is not `$vectorSearch`. src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17 defines `DBOperationArgs.database` and `CollOperationArgs.collection` as plain `z.string()` with no length cap or character allow-list, unlike `CommonArgs.string()` (args.ts:22-23), which applies `NO_UNICODE_REGEX` and is used for the Atlas tool arguments in the same repo. mcpHttpServer.ts:307 enforces express.json({limit: httpBodyLimit}) (default 100 KiB) and result-side caps (maxDocumentsPerQuery, maxBytesPerQuery) exist, but neither validates individual field length/shape, so per-field input validation is still missing. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

title: export tool writes client data to plaintext EJSON files on the host filesystem

title: MCP HTTP transport endpoint ships with no authentication, rate limiting or idempotency controls by default
description:
src/transports/mcpHttpServer.ts:306-419 exposes POST/GET/DELETE /mcp with no authentication by default: the only built-in mechanism is exact-match validation of the operator-configured httpHeaders map, which defaults to an empty object (src/common/config/userConfig.ts:136-143: httpHeaders: z.object({}).loose().default({})), so the middleware (lines 308-318) validates nothing; snippet: for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(this.userConfig.httpHeaders)) { const header = req.headers[key.toLowerCase()]; if (!header || header !== value) ... }. There is no per-request authorisation of tool calls, no rate limiter, no 429 or 409 handling, and no TLS termination in the express app. With externallyManagedSessions=true any request may supply an arbitrary mcp-session-id header and get a session without authentication (lines 336-355), after which every enabled tool (find, aggregate, insert-many, update-many, delete-many, drop-database, atlas tools) is callable against the client-data and order stores. The optional monitoring server exposes /health and /metrics unauthenticated too (src/transports/monitoringServer.ts:53-79). Deployed to prod (eks-prod-mumbai, exposure partner, data classes pii and financial) any in-cluster caller can read client data; no gateway policy (x-kong-plugin, x-amazon-apigateway-auth, Istio RequestAuthentication) exists in this repo. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17. DPDP Rule 6(1)(b) (commences 2027-05-13) is a readiness mapping. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Not refuted: every substantive claim verifies in files I opened myself — mcpHttpServer.ts:306-419 defines POST/GET/DELETE /mcp (lines 360/400/411) whose only request gate is the httpHeaders exact-match middleware at exactly 308-318 with httpHeaders defaulting to {} (userConfig.ts:136-143 verbatim, overrideBehavior not-allowed), the externallyManagedSessions implicit-session path sits at exactly 336-355, there is no rate limiter or 429/409 handling anywhere (only two app.use registrations in all of src, jsonRpcErrorCodes.ts defines none), the express app is plain HTTP with no TLS (expressBasedHttpServer.ts app.listen), monitoringServer.ts:53-79 exposes /health and /metrics with no middleware, all named tools exist (tools.ts: find/insert-many/aggregate/update-many/delete-many/drop-database plus src/tools/atlas), env/prod.json confirms eks-prod-mumbai/exposure partner/dataClassification [pii, financial], the same run's probe-iac SARIF independently shows the bicep NOAUTH default with external ingress, no ipSecurityRestrictions/WAF/rate limit (the Entra auth variant is opt-in) and no gateway-policy terms exist anywhere in the repo, all three controlIds exist as ledger control records, severity high equals the verified catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17 (the most specific Indian instrument first; dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(b) is also high and its 2027-05-13 commencement is confirmed in instruments.json line 994), the cited SARIF export exists, parses and defines rule SCH-API-01 with exactly the candidate's defaultSeverity high, severityBasis sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17 and the four regulatoryRefs, and the fingerprint matches the ledger's existing stable identity for the same ruleId+target+path (open finding fnd_01M2G2AGVRZPBP3VH8FNAYH46V, the intended re-run update); the export's minified results[] beyond the first 2000 characters of its single line, its sha256 digest and the checkout's git HEAD could not be independently opened or computed (listed unverifiable, none refuting since the export is present and the gap is confirmed in the primary source), and evidence[1] is merely a redundant duplicate of evidence[0], a style defect that does not refute.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every cited instrument applies — sebi-cscrf-2024 first as the in-scope primary for this mid-size SEBI RE (PR.AA.S17's prose squarely covers an unauthenticated, unthrottled API), dpdp-rules-2025 6(1)(b)/6(1) exist and cover access control with the 2027-05-13 commencement correctly disclosed as a readiness mapping, and the voluntary NIST/OWASP crosswalks come last — and severity high correctly equals PR.AA.S17's catalog defaultSeverity because neither the candidate nor the SARIF rule carries any CVSS/security-severity score; the only defect is repairable: owasp-asvs-5.0:8.2.1 is not the crosswalk of any cited catalog control (the SEBI catalog maps PR.AA.S17 to owasp-asvs-5.0:V4 and skills require crosswalks from catalog mappings[]), so correctedRegulatoryRefs is returned rather than refuting.).

title: zod tool-argument schemas leave database-bound input unbounded and unvalidated
description:
src/tools/args.ts:22-90: zEJSON() (lines 86-90) is z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON) - an open record with unknown values - used for every filter, pipeline, update operator and inserted document; snippet: export function zEJSON() { return z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON) as unknown as z.ZodRecord<z.ZodString, z.ZodUnknown>; }. CommonArgs.string() (lines 22-23) applies a no-Unicode regex but no maxLength; AtlasArgs.password() (lines 74-76) has min 1 max 100 and no pattern. Database and collection names are plain unbounded z.string() (src/tools/mongodb/mongodbTool.ts:11-17: database: z.string().describe("Database name")), the insert-many documents array has no maxItems (src/tools/mongodb/create/insertMany.ts:22-26), exportTitle (src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:16) and the assistant search query (src/tools/assistant/searchKnowledge.ts:9-14) are unbounded strings, and the stdio transport payload limit is informational only and not enforced (src/transports/constants.ts:15-17: 50 MiB advertised). Only the HTTP transport enforces a body limit (default 100 KiB). Oversized payloads and NoSQL operator injection through documents, filters and pipelines reach the MongoDB driver and the filesystem without schema-level constraint. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S2. DPDP Act-8(3) is a readiness mapping. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every code claim verified line-precise in the pinned checkout (args.ts:22-23 no-Unicode regex with no maxLength, 74-75 password min1/max100 without pattern, 86-90 zEJSON = z.object({}).loose().transform(toEJSON); mongodbTool.ts:11-17 unbounded database/collection z.string(); insertMany.ts:22-26 documents array without maxItems; export.ts:16 and searchKnowledge.ts:9-14 unbounded strings; constants.ts:15-17 stdio 50 MiB 'informational only' with no enforcement anywhere in stdio.ts, while mcpHttpServer.ts:307's 100 KiB express.json cap is the only enforcement — disclosed accurately by the finding); the SARIF export exists, is valid SARIF 2.1.0 from maxwell-schema-auditor 1.0.0, and defines rule SCH-API-02 at defaultSeverity medium on the stated sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.IP.S2 basis with the candidate's exact regulatoryRefs; severity medium equals PR.IP.S2's catalog defaultSeverity (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3677), dpdp-rules-2025:Act-8(3) exists in its catalog as a pre-13-May-2027 readiness control whose guidance names probe-schemas (matching the 'readiness mapping' wording), and all four instruments are in instruments.json; the repo is the deployed source for qa/prod (repo record pinned at the cited commit, env iac, bicep deploys mongodb/mongodb-mcp-server:1.11.0 built by this repo's CI) with no overlay, ignore file or central validation overriding the per-field gap; and the fingerprint is byte-identical to the open ledger finding fnd_01M2G2AGX1GZ9THG6HJ1VPP1EP for the same SCH-API-02 result at src/tools/args.ts, so this is the designed fingerprint-based re-run update rather than a duplicate (note the earlier run mapped the same fingerprint to PR.AA.S17/high, which the ledger keeper's supersession resolves); the only bytes I could not read are the gitignored export's results[] entry (single-line file truncated at char 2000, grep skips gitignored paths) and its sha256, both corroborated by the readable rule metadata, the identical prior-run fingerprint and the checkout itself — so no check under this lens fails.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every check verifiable in the workspace passed: sebi-cscrf-2024 binds example-co (active mid-size-re stock-broker and depository-participant, jurisdiction IN, in frameworksInScope) and catalog control PR.IP.S2 exists with defaultSeverity medium, matching the candidate's severity and the SARIF rule SCH-API-02's own severityBasis, and its SSDLC prose (security requirements, application security testing during development, OWASP ASVS guidance, defence in depth) is the nearest SEBI clause for an unbounded or unvalidated tool-argument schema gap since the catalog has no dedicated input-validation control; dpdp-rules-2025 also binds the company, its Act-8(3) control exists and lists probe-schemas with the candidate correctly framing it as a readiness mapping ahead of the 13 May 2027 commencement; the Indian instruments are cited first with the registry's regulators and well-formed control ids, the not-in-scope global instruments appear only as later secondary refs as the skill allows, and the patch-sla topic claim fits a vulnerability-with-a-fix; the only unverifiable pieces are the supplementary owasp-asvs-5.0:2.2.1 and nist-800-53-r5:SI-10 crosswalks (global instruments ship no catalog file), which the candidate transcribed verbatim from the rule definition in the SARIF export; note the export's rule also carries a second SEBI ref, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S17 (applies to mid-size-re, covers the OWASP API Top 10 injection angle), which the candidate may optionally add without changing severity since regulatoryRefs[0] stays PR.IP.S2.).

title: atlas-create-db-user takes a plaintext password argument and echoes the generated password back in the tool response
description:
src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts:16-20 declares password: AtlasArgs.password().nullish() (a plain z.string(), min 1 max 100, no pattern, src/tools/args.ts:74-76) and lines 89-96 echo the generated credential to the MCP client; snippet (line 93): text: `User "${username}" created successfully${shouldGeneratePassword ? ` with password: `${password}` : ""}.` Tool arguments and responses transit and are retained in the MCP client and LLM context/transcripts, so the credential leaves the gateway in plaintext. The password is registered in the session keychain only after the API call succeeds (lines 84-87), redacting later logs and telemetry but not the response itself. Compensating controls: the tool is on the default confirmationRequiredTools list and the confirmation prompt masks the password (line 109: "(Auto-generated secure password)"). Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every evidence check passed on files I opened myself: the cited SARIF export exists and contains a kind=fail result with ruleId SCH-API-06 at src/tools/atlas/create/createDBUser.ts region startLine 16 endLine 96 carrying severity high, confidence confirmed and maxwell/controlIds exactly [sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S1, dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)] with the candidate's SEBI/MeitY/OWASP/NIST refs present in the same result block; the checkout confirms every line-level fact (password: AtlasArgs.password().nullish() at createDBUser.ts:16-20, plain z.string() min 1 max 100 with no pattern at args.ts:74-76, the password echoed in the success response at 89-96 with the line-93 snippet verbatim, keychain registration at 84-87 that only feeds redaction of error messages (tool.ts:819), telemetry (telemetry.ts:342-348) and logs (loggerBase.ts:66) while the success path through invoke/appendUIResource performs no redaction), the stated compensating controls are real and accurately described (atlas-create-db-user is on the default confirmationRequiredTools list at userConfig.ts:83 and the prompt masks the password at line 109), nothing overrides the gap (deploy/ contains no readOnly or disabledTools settings), the repo is deployed in prod (partner exposure), qa and dev per env/*.json iac entries, the pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 matches the repo record, and severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json:2399) so no lower severity is warranted; note for the keeper: the ledger already holds this exact fingerprint as open finding fnd_01M2G2AGTH64FMR4XR77ZAJH7B with the same target and ruleId (narrower location 84-96), so this append should update/supersede that record rather than create a second one.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All five cited instruments apply to example-co and are ordered Indian-first (sebi-cscrf-2024 is the primary instrument for a mid-size SEBI RE per details.json entityTypes stock-broker/depository-participant and active mid-size-re registrations; dpdp-rules-2025 is in frameworksInScope and covers stock-broker; owasp-asvs-5.0 and nist-800-53-r5 are cross-sector with empty applicability), controlIds sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6, sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S1 and dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) all exist in their catalog files and cover the credential-echo gap (PR.AA.S6's guidance names probe-schemas checking credentials and probe-schemas is in its probeWorkflows; 6(1) is the umbrella safeguards control with probe-schemas in its probeWorkflows and ledger precedent on this very app), and severity high is correctly derived as the catalog defaultSeverity of regulatoryRefs[0] PR.AA.S6 per maxwell-conventions section 4 with no CVSS/security-severity score present; the only repair is that the two global crosswalks owasp-asvs-5.0:13.3.1 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5(7) come from the schema-auditor agent's rule table and are not the catalog mappings[] of the cited control, which the regulatory-catalogs skill (section 2) requires crosswalks be taken from - PR.AA.S6's mappings list owasp-asvs-5.0:V6 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5, and the ledger's own PR.AA.S6 finding for this app cited exactly V6.).

title: connect tool accepts a MongoDB connection string with embedded credentials as a plain tool argument
description:
src/tools/mongodb/connect/connect.ts:13-15 declares connectionString: z.string().describe("MongoDB connection string (in the mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// format)") with no pattern, format or secret marker; the mongodb+srv URI format embeds username:password, so the live credential is supplied through the LLM tool-call channel and persists in client transcripts. Line 43 passes it to this.session.connectToMongoDB({ connectionString }). Only config-supplied connection strings are registered for redaction (src/common/config/parseUserConfig.ts:179 and src/setup/setupMcpServer.ts:228); the tool-argument path never registers the string in the session keychain (verified: no keychain.register call on the connect path), so driver or parser error text that echoes the URI reaches the 30-day disk log unredacted. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every material claim was verified against files I opened: the SARIF export exists at the cited path and contains a SCH-API-06 result located at src/tools/mongodb/connect/connect.ts with region startLine 13 endLine 48 and carrying the candidate's exact fingerprint aeaedeb4... (the 01→02→06→06 result ordering probes are consistent with the 'result index 3' locator); connect.ts:13-15 declares connectionString as a plain z.string() with no pattern, format or secret marker and line 43 passes it to session.connectToMongoDB; keychain.register appears only on the config path (parseUserConfig.ts:179, setupMcpServer.ts:228) and never on the tool path (error redaction via keychain.allSecrets therefore cannot scrub the URI); the disk logger is enabled by default with retentionDays 30 (userConfig.ts:58, diskLogger.ts:23); no ignore file or deployment override disables the connect tool (deploy/aws/Dockerfile disables only atlas-local, MDB_MCP_READ_ONLY explicitly keeps connect, server.json documents connect as the path when MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING is unset); the repo is deployed in dev/qa/prod (env records reference its Dockerfile/deploy IaC, prod partner-exposed with pii/financial data); severity high equals the verified catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 2399) and the export contains no security-severity override; all three controlIds exist as ledger control records (dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) applicable to the mcp-gateway environments) and the export's result properties carry the same controlIds; and the fingerprint is not already used in the ledger (the prior SCH-API-06 finding fnd_01M2G2AGTH64FMR4XR77ZAJH7B is a different instance at createDBUser.ts with a different fingerprint).); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All four cited instruments exist in the vocab and apply to example-co (SEBI CSCRF is in frameworksInScope and the company is an active SEBI mid-size-re stock-broker/DP, so the most specific Indian instrument is correctly first; DPDP Rules and the two cross-sector frameworks are applicability-legal), both SEBI controls exist in the SEBI catalog and their prose covers the credential-handling gap with severity high correctly derived as the catalog defaultSeverity of regulatoryRefs[0] sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 (no CVE/CVSS or SARIF security-severity score basis exists, and the auditor's documented SCH-API-06 crosswalks are exactly owasp-asvs-5.0:13.3.1 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5(7), though the auditor's table maps this rule primarily to PR.AA.S1, which carries the same defaultSeverity), but the third ref dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) is mis-mapped and must be dropped: the DPDP catalog's own control 1 guidance forbids reporting rule 5-to-16 controls as current breaches before 13 May 2027 ("Until those dates neither the Act obligation nor the manner prescribed by these Rules is binding"), and 6(1)'s prose and guidance scope it to protecting personal data of Data Principals, which a MongoDB connection-string credential is not and which this finding never claims, so the mapping fails on that one ref yet is repaired by removing it, leaving a valid mapping on the in-force SEBI controls.).

title: switch-connection tool accepts a connection string with embedded credentials as a plain tool argument
description:
src/tools/mongodb/connect/switchConnection.ts:13-20 declares an optional connectionString: z.string() with no pattern and no secret marker (snippet: connectionString: z.string().optional().describe("MongoDB connection string to switch to (in the mongodb:// or mongodb+srv:// format). If a connection string is not provided, the connection string from the config will be used.")) and line 51 passes it to this.session.connectToMongoDB without registering it in the session keychain - the same class of gap as the connect tool. Credentials supplied this way transit the LLM tool-call channel and persist in client transcripts; only the config-supplied connection string is redaction-registered. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6. SLA topic: patch-sla. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every claim verified in files I opened: switchConnection.ts:13-20 declares connectionString: z.string().optional() with no pattern and no secret marker (the quoted describe snippet matches the checkout verbatim) and line 51 passes it to session.connectToMongoDB, which (session.ts:148-150) does no keychain registration while the only connection-string registration is the config-supplied one (parseUserConfig.ts:179), no override neutralises the tool (userConfig.ts disabledTools defaults to [], no allowlist), the repo is deployed in dev/qa/prod (prod exposure partner) with the same pattern in connect.ts (results[3] is its SCH-API-06 fail), the SARIF export's results[4] is a fail/error SCH-API-06 result located at switchConnection.ts region 13-57 whose message names switch-connection and the keychain, and severity high matches both the rule's severityBasis and catalog sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.AA.S6 defaultSeverity (cited PR.AA.S1 and dpdp-rules-2025:6(1) also exist, Indian instruments first); only the export's sha256 could not be recomputed (listed unverifiable; the export itself is present and contains the result, so the claim stands).); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (All four cited instruments are in the vocab and applicable to example-co (sebi-cscrf-2024 covers its active stock-broker/depository-participant mid-size-re registrations and is correctly the first, most specific Indian instrument; dpdp-rules-2025 is in frameworksInScope with matching entityTypes; owasp-asvs-5.0 and nist-800-53-r5 are voluntary global crosswalks placed last and match the workflow's own SCH-API-06 rule table in .claude/agents/schema-auditor.md:186), all three control ids exist in their catalogs (PR.AA.S1 and PR.AA.S6 in sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json lines 2140/2393, 6(1) in dpdp-rules-2025.catalog.json line 564) and their prose/guidance cover the credential-management gap the checkout shows literally (switchConnection.ts:13-20 optional connectionString with no pattern or secret marker, line 51 passing it to connectToMongoDB with no keychain registration), and severity high follows maxwell-conventions section 4 step 2 exactly (no CVSS score present; PR.AA.S6 defaultSeverity is high, and the secondary PR.AA.S1 is also high so the value is stable whichever SEBI control is treated as most specific); two nuances that do not refute under this lens: DPDP Rule 6 commences only on 2027-05-13 per the registry structure note so the in-force anchor today would be dpdp-act-2023:8(5) (which the 6(1) catalog entry itself maps to), and the global crosswalks 13.3.1/IA-5(7) come from the schema-auditor rule table rather than the cited controls' catalog mappings (which list owasp-asvs-5.0:V6 and nist-800-53-r5:IA-5), neither of which changes severity or applicability (SARIF rule/result internals beyond the first 2000 chars were unreadable, see unverifiable).)

title: export tool writes query results (pii, financial) to plaintext EJSON files with no encryption or access controls
description:
src/common/exportsManager.ts:198-249: ExportsManager.startExport does fs.mkdir(this.exportsDirectoryPath, { recursive: true }) then createWriteStream(inProgressExport.exportPath) - snippet: const outputStream = createWriteStream(inProgressExport.exportPath); const ejsonTransform = this.docToEJSONStream(...); await pipeline([input.stream(), ejsonTransform, outputStream]) - with no encryption, no file-mode restriction and no vault or KMS reference. The default folder is the user home .mongodb/mongodb-mcp/exports directory (src/common/config/configUtils.ts:53-55) and each session writes under a per-session subfolder (lines 363-372). Files carry full find/aggregate documents from the client-data and order stores that env/prod.json classifies as pii and financial, are served back by resource URI and, when the server runs locally, by raw filesystem path (src/tools/mongodb/read/export.ts:119-124). Retention is a partial compensating control: exports expire after exportTimeoutMs (default 300000 ms, request overrides can only lower it) with a cleanup cycle (lines 297-338) and the folder is deleted recursively on shutdown (lines 110-126), but during their life the data sits unencrypted on the host. Severity is the catalog defaultSeverity of sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1. DPDP Rule 6(1)(a) is a readiness mapping. SLA topic: encryption. Commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0.

Refutation: evidence lens not refuted (Every evidence check passed on bytes I opened myself: the SARIF export at the cited path contains a SCH-PII-02 result at index 5 (confirmed by ruleId-chain probes: 5 ruleIds before it match, 6 do not) located at src/common/exportsManager.ts with startLine 198 and endLine 249, carrying the candidate's fingerprint value and the verbatim message phrase 'client-data and order stores', and its rule declares defaultSeverity high with severityBasis sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1; the checkout at pinned commit aaa72a040db4c32f3d6488d5e28e2892a68e9ee0 exhibits the gap exactly as described (createWriteStream with no mode option, no encryption or KMS/vault reference anywhere in the write path, exportsPath default ~/.mongodb/mongodb-mcp/exports at configUtils.ts:53-55, per-session subfolder at 363-372, resource-URI and raw-path serving at export.ts:119-124, exportTimeoutMs default 300_000 with onlyLowerThanBaseValueOverride at userConfig.ts:194-198, cleanup at 297-338 and recursive shutdown deletion at 110-126), with no overriding compensating control in the repo (chmod/umask appear only in the src/ui frontend bundle and 'encrypt' only in atlas openapi.d.ts type declarations, neither in the export path), the condition is reachable in the deployed prod environment (env/prod.json dataClassification pii+financial, partner exposure) and independently corroborated by ledger observation obs_01M2H1VF3N8NATYT9XVASD12XF, severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of PR.DS.S1 (sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3222, whose guidance prescribes high for unencrypted stores on the encryption topic) so no lower severity is supported, all cited controls exist and apply (RBI 140 is a Cryptographic Controls clause whose guidance names probe-schemas; dpdp-rules-2025:6(1)(a) is a PR.DS.S1 catalog mapping; NIST SC-28 likewise), and the fingerprint is unused elsewhere in the ledger; the only unverifiable item is the export's sha256 digest (no independent record in the workspace to compare against), and evidence[1] is a byte-identical duplicate of evidence[0] minus its description.); regulatory-mapping lens not refuted (Every cited instrument binds example-co (sebi-cscrf-2024 via active mid-size-re stock-broker/DP registrations, rbi-cyber-tech-directions-2026 via the active nbfc-middle-layer registration and in force since 2026-07-31, dpdp-rules-2025 and the global nist-800-53-r5), each controlId exists in its catalog with prose covering unencrypted pii/financial data at rest — the PR.DS.S1 guidance prescribes exactly this finding ('Each unencrypted store ... is a high finding citing sebi-cscrf-2024:PR.DS.S1, topic encryption'), RBI 140's guidance names probe-schemas checking that sensitive fields are encrypted/tokenised, and 6(1)(a) mandates encryption of personal data — the most specific Indian instrument (SEBI, the company's primary licence and the ledger's existing SCH-PII-02 control key) is first with the global crosswalk last, and severity high equals the catalog defaultSeverity of PR.DS.S1 verified at sebi-cscrf-2024.catalog.json line 3222 per maxwell-conventions section 4 (the finding carries no CVSS score and the tool's rule properties use defaultSeverity/severityBasis, not security-severity), with the 'readiness mapping' label on Rule 6(1)(a) matching the DPDP catalog's own commencement rule (rule 6 controls commence 2027-05-13; gaps before then are raised at catalog severity as readiness gaps) and 'SLA topic: encryption' being a valid vocab topic that the SEBI guidance says falls to the sla-table defaults. )
